facts.raw_span: A 48-year-old man with no prior medical history
underwent routine abdominal ultrasonography, which revealed three well-defined hypoechoic hepatic masses
in segments 1 (67×53 mm), 6 (13 mm), and 2 (9 mm)
He was asymptomatic
normal total bilirubin (0.6 mg/dL) and albumin (4.2 g/dL)
mildly elevated AST (37 IU/L), ALT (70 IU/L), ALP (176 U/L), and GGT (170 IU/L)
tumor markers, including alpha-fetoprotein (2.9 ng/mL), PIVKA-II (11 mAU/mL), and CA19-9 (4.0 IU/L), were within normal limits
Dynamic contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated a 65 mm low-density mass with an irregular margin in the caudate lobe
showing peripheral early ring enhancement in the arterial phase and heterogeneous internal enhancement in the delayed phase
EOB-MRI revealed a hypointense mass on T1-weighted images containing several hyperintense areas on T2-weighted images
the lesion remained hypointense in the hepatobiliary phase
FDG-PET showed no radiotracer accumulation in any of the hepatic lesions
Gastroscopy and colonoscopy were unremarkable
